chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Saeed, from Suleyman al-Ja'fari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:
The one familiar regarding the chess is like the one familiar regarding the Fire.

key_terms.الْمُطَّلِعُ: The one familiar / The one acquainted

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of chess in Shia hadith literature?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) equates familiarity with chess (al-shatranj) to familiarity with the Hellfire, a metaphor rooted in the pre-Islamic Arab belief that the game was invented by Iblis as a tool for distraction and spiritual neglect. This comparison underscores the risk of the game leading to the neglect of obligatory prayers (salat) and dhikr, thereby serving as a gateway to divine punishment.

en.hubeali:
Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Saeed, from Suleyman Al Ja’fary, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one familiar regarding the chess is like the one familiar regarding the Fire’.
en.sarwar: 16. Sahl ibn Ziyad has narrated from Ali ibn Sa‘id from Sulayman al-Ja‘fariy who has said the following: “Abu al-Hassan, al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
One who seeks cognizance with chess is like one seeking cognizance with the fire.’”
